c.title: Proposal 2026-1
c.pre: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
c.q: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?

c.title: Proposal 2026-2
c.pre: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
c.q:
The proposal would:

• Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them.

• Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them.

• Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: WATERVLIET JOINT FIRE DEPARTMENT MILLAGE PROPOSAL
c.q: Shall the expired, previous voted increase in the tax limitation, on the total amount of taxes which may be assessed against all taxable valuation of all property in Watervliet City liable for taxation, of 1.9712 mills ($1.97 per each $1,000.00 of taxable value), and unchanged by the required millage rollbacks be renewed at up to 1.9712 mills ($1.9712 per each $1,000.00 of taxable valuation) and levied for a period of two years, 2027 through 2028, inclusive, for the purpose of supporting fire protection services in the City of Watervliet, raising an estimated $93,356.69 in the first year the millage is levied.

c.title: PROPOSAL TO LIMIT THE NUMBER OF MARIHUANA RETAILERS IN THE CITY OF NILES
c.q:
It is proposed that the City of Niles Code of Ordinances, Section 54-534(a)(1) be amended to add the following the language:

(b) Notwithstanding 54-534(a)(1)(a), a maximum of five marihuana retailers as defined in MCL 333.27953(q) are permitted in the city.

Should this proposed amendment be adopted?

c.title: RENEWAL OF EMERGENCY SERVICES MILLAGE FOR POLICE, FIRE &
c.q: In support of the continued operation of the Village of Michiana, Berrien County, Michigan, Police, Fire & Ambulance service and continued operating expenses and equipment for Emergency Services including Police, Fire & Ambulance service, shall the Village levy 1 (one) mill which is equal to $1.00 (One Dollar) for each $1,000.00 (One Thousand Dollars) of real and personal property subject to taxation, which equals a renewal of the current millage rate of .8803 mills ($0.8803 per $1,000 of real and personal property subject to taxation) plus an increase of .1197 mills ($0.1197 per $1,000 of real and personal property subject to taxation). Said millage will be used for emergency services equipment and general operating expenses for emergency services. Said millage, if approved by the electors of the Village of Michiana, will be levied for a period of 6 (six) years, starting in 2027 and ending in 2032. It is estimated that the levy will generate approximately $112,784.20 in the first year.

c.title: Dial-A-Ride Millage Renewal
c.q: Shall the City of Buchanan be authorized to renew and levy a total of 0.80 mill on the taxable value of all taxable property in the City of Buchanan, which is equal to $.80 per each $1,000 of taxable value, for the purpose of providing public transportation including the operation of the "Dial-A-Ride" Bus System, currently operated by Niles Dial-A-Ride, more commonly known as "DART," and more properly known as the "Dial-A-Ride Transportation System," for a period of four (4) consecutive years, to be levied in 2027, 2028, 2029, and 2030? The amount of revenue generated in the first year of the levy (2027) will be approximately $96,039.00. The proposed millage is a renewal of a previously authorized millage.

c.title: A PROPOSAL TO AMEND THE BENTON HARBOR CITY CHARTER TO ESTABLISH A BENTON HARBOR HEALTH EQUALITY COMMITTEE AND REQUIRE A HEALTHCARE ACTION PLAN
c.q:
A proposal to amend the Benton Harbor City Charter to establish a Benton Harbor Health Equality Committee appointed by the City Commission to address health care affordability and access. The Committee would gather public testimony from the community; analyze data; review how federal, state, and local policies have affected healthcare affordability and access; and produce a biennial Healthcare Action Plan. The Healthcare Action Plan would evaluate changes in health insurance and benefit coverage, track actions of federal and state officials, and recommend solutions. The City Commission would adopt and publish a Healthcare Action Plan.

Shall this proposal be adopted?

c.title: DIAL-A-RIDE (TCATA) TWIN CITIES AREA TRANSIT AUTHORITY MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: Shall the City of Benton Harbor renew a levy of 1.1568 mills on all real and tangible personal property in the City of Benton Harbor for the exclusive purpose of financing the contractual obligation created by the contract between the City of Benton Harbor and Twin Cities Area Transportation Authority (Dial-a-Ride) for a period of twenty (20) years, 2028 through 2047. The estimated revenue collected in the first year is approximately $225,137

c.title: Niles Charter Township Marihuana Retail Establishments Ordinance
c.q:
NILES CHARTER TOWNSHIP ORDAINS:

Section 1. Effective Date and Scope. This ordinance shall take effect immediately after certification of the election at which it is approved by the electors. The scope of this ordinance is limited to providing for the number of Marijuana Establishments allowed to operate in the township at any one time.

Section 2. Amendment or Repeal. On and after the effective date of the Local Marijuana Control Ordinance, any existing ordinances, resolutions, parts of ordinances or sections in conflict with provisions of this ordinance, and specifically the “Niles Charter Township Prohibition of Marijuana Establishment Ordinance” would be amended or repealed only to the extent necessary to give this proposed ordinance full force and effect.

Section 3. Four Marijuana Retail Establishments Allowed. Four (4) Adult Use retail marihuana establishments are allowed to operate within the township at any one time.

Shall this Ordinance be approved?

c.title: LIBRARY MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: In support of the continued operation of the Bridgman City Library, shall the limitation on the total amount of taxes which may be assessed against the taxable valuation of all real and personal property in the City of Bridgman liable for taxation be set at one (1) mill ($1.00 per each $1,000 of taxable valuation), which includes a renewal of .9419 mills ($0.9419 per each $1,000 of taxable valuation) plus an increase of .0581 mills ($.0581 per each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The authorization to renew the levy of said millage shall be for a period of five (5) years, being the years 2028 through 2032. It is estimated that the amount of revenue to be generated from the total millage in the first year of levy (2028) will be approximately $155,562.31.

c.title: BRIDGMAN PUBLIC LIBRARY MILLAGE PROPOSAL- HEADLEE OVERRIDE
c.q: In support of the continued operation of the Bridgman Public Library, shall the limitation on the total amount of taxes which may be assessed against the taxable valuation of all real and personal property in the City of Bridgman liable for taxation be set at one (1) mill ($1.00 per each $1,000 of taxable valuation), which includes a current Charter millage for the Bridgman Public Library of .6919 mills ($0.6919 per each $1,000 of taxable valuation) plus an increase of .3081 mills ($.3081 per each $1,000 of taxable valuation) to override the Headlee reductions to the current Library Millage and bring the total amount of the Library Millage to one (1) mill? The authorization for the additional proposed Library Millage is of a perpetual duration and would raise approximately $48,887.32 in the first year of levy (2027).

c.title: SODUS TOWNSHIP PROPOSAL
c.q: Shall the expired previous voted increase in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Sodus Township, of 2 mills ($2.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value on real and personal property), reduced to 1.9387 mills ($1.9387 per $1,000.00 of taxable value on both real and personal property) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at and increased up to the original voted 2.0 mills ($2.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value on real and personal property) and levied for four (4) years, 2027 through 2030, inclusive, for the continued maintenance and improvements to the roads of Sodus Township, raising an estimated $205,000.00 in the first year the millage is levied.

c.title: LINCOLN TOWNSHIP POLICE DEPARTMENT MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: Shall the previously approved increase in the tax limitation imposed by Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in the Charter Township of Lincoln of 1.50 mills, reduced to 1.4706 mills by required rollbacks, be renewed and replaced at up to 1.4706 mills ($1.4706 per $1,000 of taxable value), and levied for a period of 10 years, 2026 through 2035, inclusive, for the purposes of operating the Lincoln Township Police Department, raising an estimated $1,412,749 in the first year the millage is levied. This renewal will replace the existing Lincoln Township Police Department Millage set to expire in 2027 and will be levied beginning December 2026.

c.title: LINCOLN TOWNSHIP ROAD MAINTENANCE MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: Shall the previously approved increase in the tax limitation imposed by Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in the Charter Township of Lincoln of .25 mills, reduced to .2449 mills by required rollbacks, be renewed at up to .2449 mills ($.2449 per $1,000 of taxable value), and levied for a period of 6 years, 2026 through 2031, inclusive, for the purposes of maintenance, repair and replacement of the public roads in Lincoln Charter Township, raising an estimated $235,266 in the first year the millage is levied. This renewal will replace the existing Lincoln Township Road Maintenance Millage set to expire in 2027 and will be levied beginning December 2026.

c.title: VILLAGE OF BARODA DISINCORPORATION
c.q: Shall incorporation of the Village of Baroda be vacated?

c.title: NEW PUBLIC SAFETY MILLAGE TO FUND BARODA TOWNSHIP POLICE SERVICES
c.q: In support of the continued operation of the Baroda-Lake Police Department, and in order to keep providing full time police services to Baroda Township residents, shall the limitation on the total amount of taxes which may be assessed under Article XI, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution against the taxable valuation of all real and personal property in Baroda Township liable for taxation, including that land and personal property lying in the Village of Baroda, be increased by a new millage of 1.3601 mills ($1.3601 per $1,000 of taxable valuation, as equalized). The authorization to levy said millage is for a period of four (4) years, being the years of 2027 through 2030. It is estimated that the amount of revenue to be generated from the 1.3601-mills in the first year of levy will be approximately $195,150.68.

c.title: Public Safety Millage
c.q: In support of Public Safety Services, including Fire, Police and Ambulance Services, shall the City of Coloma be authorized to levy a new city-wide millage, totaling 1.0 mills ($1.00 per each $1,000.00 of taxable value), against all taxable valuation of property in the City of Coloma liable for taxation, and levied for a period of 20 years, 2026 through 2045 inclusive, for the purpose of supporting Public Safety Services in the City of Coloma, raising an estimated $45,765 in the first year the millage is levied.

c.title: COLOMA COMMUNITY SCHOOLS SINKING FUND MILLAGE RENEWAL PROPOSAL
c.q:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the building and site sinking fund millage that expires with the 2027 tax levy.

Shall the currently authorized millage rate of 1.1825 mills ($1.1825 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) which may be assessed against all property in Coloma Community Schools, Berrien and Van Buren Counties, Michigan, be renewed for a period of 10 years, 2028 to 2037, inclusive, to continue to provide for a sinking fund for the purchase of real estate for sites for, and the construction or repair of, school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; and all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2028 is approximately $658,517 (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2027 tax levy)?

c.title: PROPOSAL FOR ROAD MILLAGE
c.q: Shall Berrien Township impose an increase of up to 7/8 mill ($0.875 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for four years, 2027 through 2030 inclusive, for road maintenance, repair and construction, raising an estimated $200,672.00 in the first year the millage is levied? This millage will replace the current road assessment for road maintenance, repair and construction which will expire in 2026.

c.title: ROYALTON TOWNSHIP
c.q: Shall the tax limitation on all taxable property within Royalton Township, Berrien County, Michigan, be increased and the Township be authorized to levy annually a new millage in the amount of 0.4 mills ($0.40 per $1,000 of taxable value), for four years, 2027 to 2030 inclusive, to provide funds for Township library services? The estimated revenue the Township will collect in the first year of levy (2027) if the millage is approved is approximately $155,018. To the extent required by law, a portion of the revenues collected from this millage (estimated to be approximately 1.2% in the first year), will be captured by or disbursed to the Berrien County Brownfield Redevelopment Authority.

c.title: ROYALTON TOWNSHIP
c.pre: SPECIAL ASSESSMENT FOR TOWNSHIP AMBULANCE SERVICES
c.q: Should Royalton Township, Berrien County, Michigan, pursuant to Section 20948 of the Public Health Code, Act 368 of the Michigan Public Acts, 1978, as amended, and Public Act 33 of the Michigan Public Acts, 1951, as amended, MCL 41.801 et. seq., raise money to equip, maintain and operate or to contract for, ambulance services by annual special assessments levies of up to 0.75 mill ($0.75 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) on all real property in the Township that is not exempt from property taxes, for a period of ten (10)years, with the levies to be from 2027 to 2036, to provide funding for the 2027 to 2036 calendar years? If approved and fully levied in December 2027, the estimated revenue from this special assessment collected in the first year would be $290,658.00.

c.title: ROYALTON TOWNSHIP
c.pre: SPECIAL ASSESSMENT TO EQUIP, MAINTAIN AND OPERATE TOWNSHIP FIRE DEPARTMENT
c.q: Should Royalton Township, Berrien County, Michigan, pursuant to Public Act 33 of the Michigan Public Acts, 1951, as amended, MCL 41.801 et. seq., raise money to equip, maintain, and operate the Township Fire Department by annual special assessments levies of up to 1.25 mills ($1.25 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) on all real property in the Township that is not exempt from property taxes, for a period of ten (10) years, with the levies to be from 2027 to 2036, to provide funding for the 2027 to 2036 calendar years,? If approved and fully levied in December 2027, the estimated revenue from this special assessment collected in the first year would be $484,430.00.
